severityMethod.name: OWASP Risk Rating Methodology
severityMethod.summary: Threats and vulnerabilities are scored for impact and likelihood (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) with a written rationale. Overall severity is read from the OWASP Risk Rating matrix. A guardrail's severity is the highest severity among the risks it directly mitigates.

Autonomous Agent & MCP Security.summary: Agents that call tools and run code on your behalf: hijacked tool calls, code execution, manipulated human approvals, and agents that go rogue.

RAG & Knowledge Retrieval Security.summary: Chatbots that answer from your documents: poisoned sources, injected instructions, leaked files, and embeddings that give away their source text.

Model Supply Chain & Training Integrity.summary: Where your model, data, and code come from: poisoned training sets, malicious model files, hallucinated packages, and memorized secrets.

LLM Application & Output Security.summary: The app around the model: leaked prompts, jailbreaks, data-stealing output, confident wrong answers, and runaway costs.

Multi-Agent & Memory Trust.summary: Agents that remember and talk to each other: poisoned memory, tampered tools, impersonation, and failures that cascade.

paths.title: Securing an MCP-connected agent
paths.summary: For teams giving an agent tools through MCP servers. Covers what a malicious tool can do and the controls that contain it.

steps.note: Start with the tools themselves: an MCP server can hide instructions in tool descriptions.
This works because clients trust tool definitions that can change after you approve them.
Fix: pin tool definitions by hash and require re-approval when they change.
Even with trusted tools, injected text can steer which tool runs and with what arguments.
The damage depends on how much each tool is allowed to do.
Fix: give each tool the narrowest token it needs, for the shortest time.
Fix: require approval from a separate reviewer before high-impact actions run.

paths.title: Hardening a RAG chatbot
paths.summary: For teams answering questions from internal documents. Follows a poisoned document from ingestion to a leaked answer.

steps.note: Any document you index can carry instructions aimed at the model.
They reach the model because retrieved text is pasted into the prompt as-is.
Fix: scan and quarantine documents before they are indexed.
Separately, the chatbot may answer with documents the user isn't allowed to see.
This happens when one index mixes documents with different access levels.
Fix: filter search results by the user's permissions before the model sees them.
Finally, injected instructions can make the answer itself leak data when rendered.
Fix: sanitize output and block remote images with a strict CSP.

paths.title: Bringing in an open-weights model
paths.summary: For teams downloading models or fine-tuning on outside data. Covers the checks to run before a model reaches production.

steps.note: A downloaded model file can run code the moment you load it.
The cause is pickle-based loading of untrusted files.
Fix: load only tensor-only formats and scan uploads.
Fix: promote only signed, hash-pinned artifacts with a bill of materials.
Fine-tuning data can also plant hidden behavior.
Fix: track where every dataset came from and screen it before training.

paths.title: Keeping an autonomous agent under control
paths.summary: For teams letting agents run code or take actions. Covers code execution, human approvals, and stopping an agent that goes wrong.

steps.note: Agents that can run code turn a prompt injection into remote code execution.
The root cause is running model-generated code where secrets and the network are reachable.
Fix: run generated code in a throwaway sandbox with no credentials and no outbound network.
Human approval is the next line of defense, but a steered agent can talk reviewers into saying yes.
Fix: show reviewers the exact action and its effect, generated by the system rather than the agent.
If an agent is compromised anyway, the question becomes how fast you notice and stop it.
Fix: log every step, detect scope drift, and keep a tested kill switch.

paths.title: Shipping answers people can trust
paths.summary: For teams whose users act on AI answers. Covers hallucinations, overreliance, and the attacks that exploit them.

steps.note: The model will sometimes state false things confidently, and users may act on them.
This is worst when answers come from model memory with nothing to check them against.
Fix: answer from trusted sources and verify every citation before showing it.
Fix: label AI output and send high-stakes questions to a human.
Attackers also exploit hallucinations directly, by registering package names that assistants invent.
Fix: install only from an approved registry so invented names cannot resolve to malware.

nodes.title: Agent Tool Hijacking
nodes.summary: Adversary steers an autonomous agent into invoking privileged tools with attacker-chosen arguments via prompt or memory manipulation.

risk.rationale: Impact high: privileged tools act on production systems. Likelihood high: any untrusted text in context can carry the payload, and public demonstrations are routine.

nodes.impact: Unauthorized tool execution can exfiltrate secrets, mutate production systems, or pivot into connected SaaS APIs.
remediation: Bind every tool call to an allowlisted schema and deny unknown parameters.
Require human approval for high-impact tools (write, delete, payment, admin).
Isolate tool credentials per agent session with short-lived tokens.
verification: Red-team with tool-name confusion and argument smuggling payloads.
Assert audit logs capture caller identity, tool name, and argument digests.
nodes.codeExample:
if (!allowlist.has(tool.name)) throw new DenyError('tool');
validate(tool.args, schemas[tool.name]);

nodes.title: Unbounded MCP Tool Calls
nodes.summary: Model Context Protocol servers expose tools without rate, depth, or blast-radius limits, enabling recursive or fan-out abuse.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: cost and availability loss, usually recoverable. Likelihood high: agent loops occur even without an attacker.

nodes.impact: Runaway tool loops burn budget, overwhelm backends, and amplify a single injection into multi-system damage.
remediation: Enforce per-session call budgets and maximum recursion depth.
Circuit-break on repeated identical tool invocations.
Scope MCP servers to least-privilege resource sets.
verification: Load-test agent loops against a mock MCP server with budget counters.
Confirm circuit breakers trip before backend SLOs are breached.

nodes.title: Goal Alignment Drift
nodes.summary: Long-running agents gradually reinterpret objectives after poisoned memory, competing rewards, or multi-turn adversarial framing.

risk.rationale: Impact high: agent acts against policy while appearing healthy. Likelihood medium: needs long-running memory or multi-turn access.

nodes.impact: Agents pursue shadow goals that violate policy while still appearing task-complete in telemetry.
remediation: Checkpoint goals against a signed policy charter each turn.
Separate planner and executor agents with dual-approval on goal changes.
Expire and re-hash agent memory entries with integrity checks.
verification: Inject contradictory goal updates mid-run and confirm charter veto.
Review divergence metrics between declared goal and tool sequence.

nodes.title: Excessive Tool Permissions
nodes.summary: MCP tools and agent connectors inherit broad OAuth scopes or filesystem rights far beyond the task need.

risk.rationale: Impact high: one bad call inherits admin reach. Likelihood high: broad OAuth scopes are the default in most connectors.

nodes.impact: A single compromised tool call inherits admin-level reach across mail, cloud storage, and CI.
remediation: Issue narrowly scoped tokens per tool capability.
Prefer ephemeral credentials minted at invocation time.
Deny-by-default filesystem and network egress for sandboxed runtimes.
verification: Enumerate effective scopes in a pre-deploy permission report.
Attempt out-of-scope API calls and expect hard denials.
nodes.codeExample: const token = mint({ scopes: tool.requiredScopes, ttl: '90s' });

nodes.title: Unvalidated Function Arguments
nodes.summary: Tool handlers accept free-form model output without schema, type, or semantic validation before execution.

risk.rationale: Impact high: arguments reach SQL, shell, or APIs. Likelihood medium: many frameworks validate types but not semantics.

nodes.impact: Injection payloads travel as tool arguments into SQL, shell, or privileged APIs.
remediation: Validate every argument against a JSON Schema or protobuf contract.
Reject unexpected keys and coerce enums to closed sets.
Sanitize path and URL arguments with allowlisted hosts.
verification: Fuzz tool endpoints with type-confused and nested payload corpora.
Ensure schema failures never reach side-effecting code.
nodes.codeExample:
const args = ToolSchema.parse(raw);
if (args.path.includes('..')) throw new DenyError('path');

nodes.title: Dynamic Code Execution
nodes.summary: Agents evaluate model-generated code or shell snippets in-process without a sandbox boundary.

risk.rationale: Impact high: host compromise. Likelihood high: code-interpreter tools are common and often run in-process.

nodes.impact: Arbitrary code execution yields host compromise, credential theft, and lateral movement.
remediation: Run generated code only inside ephemeral containers with no secrets mounted.
Disable network egress unless explicitly gated.
Prefer declarative tool APIs over eval/exec pathways.
verification: Attempt breakout payloads (env dump, socket open) inside the sandbox.
Confirm host PID namespace and secrets are unreachable.
nodes.codeExample: await sandbox.run(code, { network: false, mounts: [], timeoutMs: 5000 });

nodes.title: MCP Permission Scoping
nodes.summary: Least-privilege capability tokens and server-side allowlists constrain every MCP tool invocation.
nodes.impact: Limits blast radius when an agent is steered into hostile tool use.
remediation: Map each tool to a capability profile (read / write / admin).
Rotate short-lived tokens per session and revoke on anomaly.
Publish a permission matrix reviewed in change control.
verification: CI gate fails if a tool requests scopes outside its profile.
Runtime denies cross-profile invocations with auditable events.
nodes.codeExample:
assertScopes(session.token, tool.profile);
await invoke(tool, args);

nodes.title: Dual-Agent Approval Loop
nodes.summary: A separate verifier agent (or human) must approve high-risk tool plans before the executor proceeds.
nodes.impact: Blocks single-pass goal drift and tool hijacking from completing silently.
remediation: Route write/admin tools through an approval queue with TTL.
Use a differently prompted verifier model without tool credentials.
Escalate unresolved disputes to a human operator.
verification: Simulate hijack plans and confirm executor stalls until approval.
Measure false-approve rate on a labeled red-team set.
nodes.codeExample:
const verdict = await verifier.review(plan);
if (verdict !== 'ALLOW') return hold(plan);

nodes.title: Deterministic Tool Schema Validation
nodes.summary: Hard schema gates reject malformed or semantically illegal tool arguments before any side effect.
nodes.impact: Removes entire classes of argument-injection failures at the boundary.
remediation: Generate schemas from typed tool definitions; never hand-edit twice.
Log and metric schema rejection rates as a detection signal.
Version schemas and reject clients on major mismatch.
verification: Property-test schemas against adversarial JSON corpora.
Ensure zero side effects on validation failure paths.
nodes.codeExample: const parsed = z.object({ id: z.uuid(), op: z.enum(OPS) }).parse(input);

nodes.title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Documents
nodes.summary: Malicious instructions embedded in ingested files or web pages override system intent when retrieved into context.

risk.rationale: Impact high: retrieved text can redirect tools and leak data. Likelihood high: anyone who can write a document or web page reaches the context.

nodes.impact: Retrieved content becomes an untrusted instruction channel that can exfiltrate data or redirect agent tools.
remediation: Treat all retrieved text as untrusted data, never as system instructions.
Strip or quarantine instruction-like spans during pre-ingestion.
Use dual-LLM patterns: one model extracts facts, another answers without tool rights.
verification: Plant hidden instruction payloads in PDF/HTML fixtures and confirm quarantine.
Assert tool-calling models never receive raw retrieved blobs as system prompts.
nodes.codeExample:
const safe = sanitizeRetrieved(chunks); // data channel only
answer = llm.chat({ system: POLICY, data: safe });

nodes.title: Vector DB Poisoning
nodes.summary: Attacker inserts or replaces embeddings so retrieval preferentially surfaces adversarial or false content.

risk.rationale: Impact high: answers are steered at scale. Likelihood medium: requires write access to a source the index ingests.

nodes.impact: Downstream answers and agent decisions are steered by poisoned neighbors in embedding space.
remediation: Sign and version every indexed document; reject unsigned upserts.
Anomaly-detect sudden neighborhood density around new vectors.
Segment indexes by trust tier and never mix public crawl with internal ACL data.
verification: Attempt unauthorized upserts without signing keys.
Monitor recall drift on a golden query set after each reindex.

nodes.title: Unauthorized Document Exfiltration
nodes.summary: RAG answers or agent tools leak restricted documents to users who lack ACL entitlement.

risk.rationale: Impact high: regulated or confidential data leaves the boundary. Likelihood high: any authenticated user can ask.

nodes.impact: Confidential IP, PII, or regulated records leave the trust boundary through natural-language answers.
remediation: Enforce document-level ACLs at retrieval time, not only at UI login.
Redact PII in outputs with policy-aware filters.
Block citation of documents outside the requester's clearance.
verification: Cross-tenant retrieval tests must return empty hit sets.
PII canaries in indexed docs must not appear in unauthorized answers.

nodes.title: Lack of Context Sanitization
nodes.summary: Retrieved chunks are concatenated into prompts without stripping control tokens, markup, or instruction markers.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: enables injection but does not by itself grant privileges. Likelihood high: raw chunk concatenation is the default pattern.

nodes.impact: Untrusted document content is interpreted as higher-privilege instructions.
remediation: Normalize encodings and strip HTML/script before chunking.
Wrap retrieved text in explicit data delimiters the model is trained/instructed to ignore as commands.
Score and drop chunks with high instruction-likeness.
verification: Corpus of injection fixtures must be neutralized or quarantined.
Unit tests assert delimiter integrity around every chunk.
nodes.codeExample: chunks = chunks.map(c => `<DATA>\n${stripControls(c)}\n</DATA>`);

nodes.title: Over-Privileged Retrieval Indexing
nodes.summary: A shared vector index mixes clearance levels, so any authenticated user can retrieve neighbors from restricted corpora.

risk.rationale: Impact high: cross-tenant leakage. Likelihood high: single shared indexes are common in early deployments.

nodes.impact: Authorization is deferred to the chat UI while the retrieval plane already leaked candidates.
remediation: Partition indexes by tenant and clearance.
Filter candidates with ACL checks before ranking.
Never embed secrets or credentials into searchable text.
verification: Negative ACL tests across every index partition.
Secrets scanners fail the build if credentials appear in chunk text.

nodes.title: Missing Document ACLs
nodes.summary: Source documents lack enforceable ownership metadata propagated into the retrieval and citation path.

risk.rationale: Impact high: access cannot be enforced downstream. Likelihood medium: many sources already carry ACLs that are simply dropped.

nodes.impact: Access decisions cannot be evaluated consistently across ingest, retrieve, and answer stages.
remediation: Require ACL metadata at ingest; reject documents without owners.
Propagate ACL tags onto every chunk and citation.
Re-evaluate ACLs on answer rendering, not only on search.
verification: Ingest pipeline rejects ACL-less fixtures.
Citation renderer drops links the caller cannot open.
nodes.codeExample: if (!doc.acl?.owners?.length) throw new IngestError('acl-required');

nodes.title: Pre-Ingestion Scanning Pipeline
nodes.summary: Documents are scanned for injection markers, malware, and policy violations before embeddings are written.
nodes.impact: Stops poisoned or instruction-laden content from entering the retrieval corpus.
remediation: Run static detectors for instruction phrases and hidden text layers.
Quarantine failures into a review queue instead of indexing.
Re-scan on every document version bump.
verification: Known-bad fixtures never reach the production index.
Quarantine SLAs and reviewer audit trails are intact.
nodes.codeExample:
const report = await scan(doc);
if (report.risk >= 'HIGH') return quarantine(doc, report);

nodes.title: Document-Level Access Enforcement
nodes.summary: Retrieval and citation paths enforce per-document ACLs tied to the authenticated principal.
nodes.impact: Prevents unauthorized document exfiltration through RAG answers.
remediation: Filter search hits with `canRead(user, doc)` before LLM context assembly.
Bind citations to the same ACL check used for download.
Log denied retrievals for detection analytics.
verification: Cross-user retrieval suites return zero unauthorized hits.
Denied events appear in SIEM with doc id and principal.
nodes.codeExample: hits = hits.filter(h => acl.canRead(user, h.docId));

nodes.title: Output Filtering & PII Anonymization
nodes.summary: Post-generation filters redact PII, secrets, and out-of-policy content before the response is delivered.
nodes.impact: Provides a last line of defense when retrieval or generation still surfaces sensitive spans.
remediation: Run deterministic PII/secret detectors on every completion.
Replace matches with typed placeholders and log redaction counts.
Block responses that fail policy classifiers above threshold.
verification: Canary SSNs and API keys never leave the filter unmasked.
Redaction metrics alert on sudden spikes.
nodes.codeExample: return redact(completion, { pii: true, secrets: true });

nodes.title: Training & Fine-Tune Data Poisoning
nodes.summary: Adversary seeds pre-training, fine-tuning, or RLHF data with crafted samples that implant backdoors or skew behavior.

risk.rationale: Impact high: backdoors survive into production and evade evals. Likelihood medium: requires influence over a training or fine-tune source.

nodes.impact: A trigger phrase silently flips model behavior in production, bypassing safety tuning and evading standard evals.
remediation: Track provenance for every dataset shard and fine-tune contribution.
Deduplicate and outlier-filter training data before each run.
Hold out trigger-hunting and behavioral-diff evals between model versions.
verification: Train a canary model on a planted-trigger fixture and confirm detectors flag it.
Compare refusal and toxicity rates against the previous release on a frozen suite.

nodes.title: Malicious Model Artifacts
nodes.summary: Downloaded model weights or adapters carry executable payloads via unsafe serialization formats such as pickle.

risk.rationale: Impact high: code execution on training or serving hosts. Likelihood high: malicious pickles on public model hubs are repeatedly reported.

nodes.impact: Loading the model executes attacker code on training clusters or inference hosts with access to data and credentials.
remediation: Load only tensor-only formats (safetensors, GGUF) from untrusted sources.
Pin model revisions by content hash, never by mutable tag.
Scan artifacts in an isolated job before promotion to the registry.
verification: Attempt to load a pickle with an os.system payload and expect a hard failure.
Registry rejects artifacts whose digest differs from the signed manifest.
nodes.codeExample: model = load_file('model.safetensors')  # never torch.load(untrusted)

nodes.title: Model Extraction via Inference API
nodes.summary: Attacker issues high-volume, structured queries to reconstruct model behavior or distill a functional copy.

risk.rationale: Impact high: loss of model IP and a surrogate for further attacks. Likelihood medium: needs sustained, high-volume API access.

nodes.impact: Loss of proprietary model IP and a white-box surrogate that accelerates adversarial attacks.
remediation: Enforce per-key query quotas and anomaly detection on query distribution.
Return only the fields callers need; suppress logprobs by default.
Watermark outputs to support attribution of distilled copies.
verification: Replay a synthetic extraction workload and confirm throttling triggers.
Verify logprob and embedding endpoints require elevated scopes.

nodes.title: Unsafe Model Deserialization
nodes.summary: Pipelines call pickle-based loaders on third-party checkpoints, tokenizers, or LoRA adapters.

risk.rationale: Impact high: loading becomes remote code execution. Likelihood high: pickle-based loaders remain the default in many pipelines.

nodes.impact: Model loading becomes a remote code execution primitive.
remediation: Ban torch.load / pickle.load on untrusted input via lint rules.
Convert legacy checkpoints to safetensors in a sandbox once, then pin.
Set weights_only=True where pickle cannot yet be removed.
verification: Static analysis fails CI on banned loader calls.
Sandbox conversion jobs have no network or secret mounts.
nodes.codeExample: torch.load(path, weights_only=True)

nodes.title: Unverified Data & Model Provenance
nodes.summary: Datasets, base models, and adapters are pulled from public hubs without signatures, hashes, or an AI bill of materials.

risk.rationale: Impact high: compromised components cannot be traced. Likelihood medium: exploiting it still requires a poisoned upstream artifact.

nodes.impact: Teams cannot tell which upstream component introduced a backdoor or license violation.
remediation: Maintain an AIBOM listing every dataset, model, and adapter with digests.
Mirror approved artifacts into an internal registry.
Require signed attestations for third-party components.
verification: Every deployed model resolves to a complete AIBOM entry.
Builds fail when an artifact lacks a matching signature.

nodes.title: Unrestricted Inference Endpoints
nodes.summary: Inference APIs expose logprobs, embeddings, or unlimited throughput to any authenticated or anonymous caller.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: enables extraction and cost abuse rather than direct compromise. Likelihood high: unthrottled endpoints are easy to find and use.

nodes.impact: Enables extraction, membership inference, and cost harvesting at scale.
remediation: Rate-limit by key, IP, and organization with burst controls.
Gate logprobs and raw embeddings behind explicit scopes.
Alert on query patterns that sweep the input space systematically.
verification: Anonymous callers receive 401 on every inference route.
Quota exhaustion returns 429 before backend saturation.

nodes.title: Signed Model Registry & AIBOM
nodes.summary: Only signed, hash-pinned artifacts with a recorded bill of materials can be promoted to training or serving.
nodes.impact: Breaks the supply-chain path from a public hub to production inference.
remediation: Sign artifacts at build time (e.g. Sigstore) and verify at load.
Record base model, datasets, and adapters in the AIBOM.
Block promotion when a dependency is revoked upstream.
verification: Tampered weights fail verification in the serving bootstrap.
AIBOM diff is attached to every model release.
nodes.codeExample:
verifySignature(artifact, trustRoot);
assert(artifact.digest === manifest.digest);

nodes.title: Safe Artifact Loading Policy
nodes.summary: Loaders accept only tensor-only formats and run first-time conversions inside an isolated sandbox.
nodes.impact: Removes deserialization RCE as a class from model pipelines.
remediation: Allowlist file extensions at the registry boundary.
Run ModelScan-style scanners on every upload.
Quarantine artifacts that contain opcodes beyond tensor data.
verification: Known-malicious pickle fixtures are rejected at upload.
Serving images contain no pickle-capable loader paths.

nodes.title: Dataset Provenance & Poison Screening
nodes.summary: Training data is traced to source, filtered for anomalies, and screened for trigger patterns before each run.
nodes.impact: Reduces the chance that a backdoor survives into a released checkpoint.
remediation: Hash and log every shard with its origin and license.
Apply spectral-signature or activation-clustering screens on fine-tune sets.
Gate releases on behavioral-diff evals against the prior model.
verification: Planted poison fixtures are flagged before training starts.
Release checklist links the provenance report for each dataset.

nodes.title: Inference Quotas & Output Watermarking
nodes.summary: Per-tenant quotas, scoped access to sensitive outputs, and watermarking deter extraction and support attribution.
nodes.impact: Raises the cost of model theft and makes distilled copies traceable.
remediation: Token-bucket limits per key and per organization.
Disable logprobs unless the caller holds a research scope.
Embed statistical watermarks in generated text where supported.
verification: Extraction simulations hit quota before reaching useful fidelity.
Watermark detector identifies outputs from a sampled corpus.
nodes.codeExample: if (!bucket.take(key, tokens)) return res.status(429).end();

nodes.title: System Prompt Extraction
nodes.summary: Users coax the model into revealing hidden instructions, embedded credentials, or business logic.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: harmful mainly when prompts hold secrets or logic. Likelihood high: extraction prompts are widely shared and cheap to try.

nodes.impact: Leaked prompts reveal guardrail logic, internal endpoints, and sometimes live secrets.
remediation: Assume the system prompt is public; keep secrets and authz logic out of it.
Enforce policy in code, not in natural-language instructions.
Detect verbatim prompt echoes in outputs.
verification: Run a prompt-extraction corpus and confirm no secrets appear.
Canary strings in the system prompt trigger alerts if emitted.

nodes.title: Jailbreak & Safety Bypass
nodes.summary: Role-play, encoding tricks, or many-shot prompting push the model past its safety policy.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: harmful output under the product's brand, usually without system compromise. Likelihood high: new bypasses appear continuously.

nodes.impact: The application produces harmful, defamatory, or policy-violating content under its own brand.
remediation: Layer input and output classifiers independent of the base model.
Cap conversation length and context stuffing for untrusted users.
Continuously red-team against fresh jailbreak corpora.
verification: Track attack success rate per release on a frozen jailbreak suite.
Classifier failures are logged with full transcripts for review.

nodes.title: Output-Rendered Data Exfiltration
nodes.summary: Injected instructions make the model emit markdown images, links, or HTML that leak context to attacker URLs when rendered.

risk.rationale: Impact high: zero-click data theft. Likelihood high: markdown image rendering is enabled in many chat UIs.

nodes.impact: Chat history, documents, or tokens are sent to an attacker server with zero user clicks.
remediation: Never auto-load remote images or iframes from model output.
Restrict rendered link targets to an allowlist of domains.
Treat model output as untrusted input to the frontend.
verification: Plant an image-exfil payload and confirm no outbound request occurs.
CSP violation reports stay at zero in production.

nodes.title: Secrets & Policy in System Prompt
nodes.summary: API keys, internal URLs, or access rules are embedded directly in prompts the model can repeat.

risk.rationale: Impact high: live credentials exposed. Likelihood medium: requires both a secret in the prompt and a successful extraction.

nodes.impact: One successful extraction exposes credentials and reveals how to bypass controls.
remediation: Move secrets to server-side tool handlers.
Express authorization as code paths, not instructions.
Scan prompt templates for credential patterns in CI.
verification: Secret scanners run on prompt template directories.
Prompt templates contain no hostnames outside an allowlist.

nodes.title: Unsanitized Output Rendering
nodes.summary: Frontends render model output as raw HTML or markdown with remote resources enabled.

risk.rationale: Impact high: XSS and exfiltration. Likelihood high: markdown renderers load remote images by default.

nodes.impact: XSS, CSRF, and zero-click exfiltration through the chat UI.
remediation: Render with a sanitizer that strips scripts, event handlers, and remote images.
Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy on chat surfaces.
Proxy or block external URLs in generated links.
verification: XSS payload corpus produces no script execution.
Browser tests confirm img-src blocks non-allowlisted hosts.
nodes.codeExample: html = DOMPurify.sanitize(marked(output), { FORBID_TAGS: ['img', 'iframe'] });

nodes.title: Single-Layer Safety Reliance
nodes.summary: The application relies solely on the base model's alignment with no independent input or output checks.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: widens exposure to jailbreaks. Likelihood medium: base models resist many, but not all, known attacks.

nodes.impact: Any jailbreak that beats the base model reaches users unfiltered.
remediation: Add independent moderation on both input and output.
Define application-specific deny policies beyond vendor defaults.
Fail closed when the classifier is unavailable.
verification: Disabling the classifier service blocks responses rather than passing them.
Policy suite covers app-specific harms, not only generic ones.

nodes.title: Output Encoding & Strict CSP
nodes.summary: Model output is sanitized and rendered under a Content-Security-Policy that forbids remote resource loads.
nodes.impact: Neutralizes markdown-image and HTML exfiltration channels regardless of injection success.
remediation: Sanitize output server-side and again at render.
Set img-src and connect-src to self plus a vetted allowlist.
Show link destinations before navigation.
verification: CSP headers present on every chat route.
Exfil fixtures produce CSP reports, not network hits.
nodes.codeExample: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'

nodes.title: Prompt Hygiene & Canary Detection
nodes.summary: System prompts carry no secrets, include canary tokens, and outputs are scanned for prompt echoes.
nodes.impact: Turns prompt leakage into a detectable, low-impact event.
remediation: Insert a unique canary string per deployment.
Block or flag completions with high overlap to the system prompt.
Review prompt templates in code review like source code.
verification: Canary appearance raises a SIEM alert within one minute.
Overlap detector blocks verbatim prompt dumps.
nodes.codeExample: if (completion.includes(CANARY) || overlap(completion, SYSTEM) > 0.6) return block();

nodes.title: Input/Output Safety Classifiers
nodes.summary: Independent classifiers screen prompts and completions against application and vendor policy.
nodes.impact: Adds a second, differently trained layer that jailbreaks must beat.
remediation: Run input screening before the main model call.
Run output screening before streaming to the user.
Tune thresholds per surface and audience.
verification: False-negative rate measured on a labeled jailbreak set each release.
Classifier latency stays within the streaming budget.

nodes.title: Persistent Memory Poisoning
nodes.summary: Attacker plants instructions or false facts in an agent's long-term memory so they replay in future sessions.

risk.rationale: Impact high: a single injection persists across sessions. Likelihood high: assistants with memory write from untrusted context by default.

nodes.impact: A one-time injection becomes a durable backdoor affecting every later conversation.
remediation: Tag every memory write with source, trust level, and author.
Require confirmation before storing instruction-like memories.
Let users inspect and delete stored memories.
verification: Inject a memory via a retrieved document and confirm it is quarantined.
Expired memories are absent from new sessions.

nodes.title: MCP Tool Description Poisoning
nodes.summary: A malicious or compromised MCP server hides instructions in tool names, descriptions, or schemas, or swaps them after approval.

risk.rationale: Impact high: hidden directives run with tool privileges. Likelihood high: MCP servers are installed from unvetted sources, with public incidents documented in ATLAS case studies.

nodes.impact: Agents follow hidden directives from tool metadata, leaking data or shadowing trusted tools.
remediation: Pin tool manifests by hash and re-approve on any change.
Show full tool descriptions to users at install time.
Namespace tools per server to prevent shadowing.
verification: Mutate a tool description post-approval and confirm the client refuses it.
Scan manifests for instruction-like text before connecting.

nodes.title: Inter-Agent Impersonation
nodes.summary: A rogue agent spoofs a trusted peer in a multi-agent system to issue tasks or receive delegated data.

risk.rationale: Impact high: delegated credentials and data reach the attacker. Likelihood medium: requires network position or a foothold among agents.

nodes.impact: Delegated credentials and sensitive results flow to an attacker-controlled agent.
remediation: Authenticate agents with workload identity, not self-declared names.
Sign task messages and verify on receipt.
Scope delegated tokens to the specific subtask.
verification: Unsigned or mis-signed task messages are rejected.
Delegated tokens fail outside their intended audience.

nodes.title: Memory Writes Without Provenance
nodes.summary: Agents persist memories from any context source with no record of where the content came from.

risk.rationale: Impact high: untrusted content becomes trusted state. Likelihood medium: depends on the memory being written from external content.

nodes.impact: Untrusted retrieved content is promoted to trusted long-term state.
remediation: Store provenance metadata alongside each memory entry.
Weight or exclude low-trust memories at recall time.
Apply TTLs and periodic integrity review.
verification: Memory store schema rejects entries missing a source field.
Recall excludes entries flagged as untrusted.
nodes.codeExample: memory.write({ text, source: ctx.origin, trust: ctx.trust, ttl: '30d' });

nodes.title: Mutable Tool Manifests
nodes.summary: MCP clients trust tool metadata fetched at runtime and do not detect changes after initial approval.

risk.rationale: Impact high: approved tools can turn malicious. Likelihood medium: requires a compromised or malicious server operator.

nodes.impact: Enables rug-pull attacks where a benign tool turns malicious after users approve it.
remediation: Hash tool definitions at approval and compare on every session.
Prompt for re-consent when a manifest changes.
Prefer servers distributed through a vetted internal registry.
verification: Manifest drift test triggers re-approval UI.
Client logs record manifest hashes per session.

nodes.title: Unauthenticated Agent Channels
nodes.summary: Agent-to-agent messages travel over channels without mutual authentication or message integrity.

risk.rationale: Impact high: task injection and data theft. Likelihood medium: requires access to the channel.

nodes.impact: Any process on the network can inject tasks or read delegated results.
remediation: Use mTLS or signed JWTs between agents.
Bind each message to sender identity and nonce.
Reject replays outside a short time window.
verification: Replayed messages are rejected after the nonce window.
Network tests confirm plaintext channels are closed.

nodes.title: Memory Provenance & Review
nodes.summary: Long-term memory stores track source and trust, expire entries, and expose them for user review.
nodes.impact: Limits how long and how widely a poisoned memory can influence behavior.
remediation: Separate memory tiers for user-stated, agent-inferred, and retrieved facts.
Never auto-store instruction-like content from untrusted tiers.
Provide a memory audit UI with delete controls.
verification: Poison fixtures in retrieved content never reach the trusted tier.
TTL sweeps run on schedule and are audited.

nodes.title: Tool Manifest Pinning & Review
nodes.summary: Tool definitions are hash-pinned at approval, scanned for hidden instructions, and re-approved on change.
nodes.impact: Stops tool poisoning and post-approval rug pulls before tools reach the model.
remediation: Compute a canonical hash of name, description, and schema.
Diff and surface changes to the user before reconnecting.
Block descriptions that address the model directly.
verification: Changed manifests never load without fresh consent.
Scanner flags fixtures containing hidden directives.
nodes.codeExample: if (sha256(canonical(tool)) !== pinned[tool.id]) return requireReapproval(tool);

nodes.title: Agent Workload Identity & Signed Tasks
nodes.summary: Each agent holds a verifiable workload identity, and every delegated task is signed and audience-scoped.
nodes.impact: Makes impersonation and task injection between agents cryptographically detectable.
remediation: Issue SPIFFE-style identities per agent workload.
Sign task envelopes and include audience and expiry.
Log delegation chains for forensic replay.
verification: Forged identities fail mutual TLS handshakes.
Delegation audit reconstructs the full chain for any task.
nodes.codeExample: verifyEnvelope(msg, { audience: SELF_ID, maxAgeSec: 60 });

nodes.title: Hallucinated Answers Acted On
nodes.summary: Users or downstream systems act on fabricated facts, citations, or policies the model states with confidence.

risk.rationale: Impact high: courts and regulators have held operators liable for chatbot statements. Likelihood medium: harm requires someone to act on an unverified answer in a consequential setting.

nodes.impact: Wrong decisions with legal, financial, or safety consequences; the operator can be held liable for what its chatbot said.
remediation: Ground answers in retrieved, trusted sources and show the citations.
Route high-stakes topics (legal, medical, financial, policy) to human review.
State the system's limits in the interface, not only in the terms of service.
verification: Track factual accuracy on a labeled question set for every release.
Spot-check production answers in high-stakes categories each week.

nodes.title: Ungrounded, Unverified Answers
nodes.summary: Responses are generated from model memory alone, with no retrieval, citation, or check that cited sources exist and support the claim.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: errors are harmful only when relied on. Likelihood high: every model hallucinates, and many apps answer without grounding.

nodes.impact: Fabricated facts and citations reach users with nothing to catch them.
remediation: Answer from retrieved documents and require a citation for each factual claim.
Verify that cited documents exist and contain the cited passage.
Let the model say it does not know; reward abstention in evals.
verification: Citation checker rejects answers whose quotes are absent from the source.
Measure unsupported-claim rate on a held-out question set.
nodes.codeExample:
const ok = claims.every(c => sources[c.ref]?.text.includes(c.quote));
if (!ok) return abstain('unsupported claim');

nodes.title: Interface Invites Overreliance
nodes.summary: The product presents AI output as authoritative: no uncertainty cues, no labels, no prompt to verify before acting.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: amplifies other errors rather than causing them. Likelihood medium: many products now label AI output, but few add friction before action.

nodes.impact: Users skip verification because the interface signals that none is needed.
remediation: Label AI-generated content and show its sources inline.
Surface confidence or coverage signals where they are meaningful.
Add friction (confirm, review) before users act on high-stakes answers.
verification: Usability tests check whether users notice and open citations.
Every AI answer surface carries an AI-generated label.

nodes.title: Grounding & Citation Verification
nodes.summary: Answers are built from retrieved sources, each claim carries a citation, and citations are checked before the answer is shown.
nodes.impact: Turns silent hallucinations into visible abstentions or checkable claims.
remediation: Retrieve from a curated, versioned knowledge base.
Check that every citation resolves and supports its claim.
Prefer 'I don't know' over an unsupported answer.
verification: Accuracy and citation-validity metrics gate each release.
Fabricated-citation fixtures are rejected by the checker.

nodes.title: Uncertainty Labeling & High-Stakes Review
nodes.summary: AI output is labeled, limits are stated where users decide, and answers in high-stakes categories go to a trained reviewer.
nodes.impact: Keeps people from acting on unverified output where errors are costly.
remediation: Classify questions by stakes and route the top tier to human review.
Show sources and an AI-generated label on every answer.
Train staff on the system's known failure modes.
verification: Review queue SLAs are met for high-stakes categories.
Audit a sample of auto-answered questions for misrouted high-stakes items.

nodes.title: Denial of Wallet & Resource Exhaustion
nodes.summary: Floods of requests, oversized inputs, or deliberately expensive prompts drive up inference cost or take the service down.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: financial and availability loss, usually recoverable. Likelihood high: pay-per-token endpoints are cheap to abuse and easy to find.

nodes.impact: Unplanned cloud bills, degraded service for legitimate users, or a full outage.
remediation: Cap input size, output tokens, and execution time per request.
Apply per-user and per-tenant quotas with budget alerts.
Degrade gracefully (shorter answers, queueing) instead of failing outright.
verification: Load-test with oversized and adversarially expensive prompts.
Confirm budget alerts fire before spend exceeds the monthly cap.

nodes.title: No Per-Request Resource Limits
nodes.summary: Requests can use unlimited context, output tokens, tool calls, or wall-clock time, and spend is not tracked per caller.

risk.rationale: Impact medium: enables cost and availability attacks. Likelihood high: default SDK settings rarely set budgets.

nodes.impact: A single caller can consume capacity and budget meant for everyone.
remediation: Set max input tokens, max output tokens, and timeouts on every call.
Meter spend per key, user, and tenant.
Limit queued and concurrent actions per session.
verification: Requests over the limit are rejected with a clear error.
Dashboards show per-tenant spend with anomaly alerts.
nodes.codeExample:
llm.create({ input, max_tokens: 1024, timeout_ms: 20000 });
meter.charge(tenant, usage.total_tokens);

nodes.title: Resource Budgets, Timeouts & Graceful Degradation
nodes.summary: Every request, session, and tenant runs within explicit token, time, and spend budgets, with a degraded mode under load.
nodes.impact: Bounds the cost and blast radius of abuse and of runaway legitimate use.
remediation: Define budgets per request, session, user, and tenant.
Alert on spend velocity, not only totals.
Fall back to cheaper models or queueing when budgets tighten.
verification: Chaos tests confirm degraded mode keeps core flows available.
Budget breaches page on-call before the monthly cap.

nodes.title: Hallucinated Package Squatting
nodes.summary: Attackers register package names that coding assistants hallucinate, so developers or agents that install the suggestion pull in malware.

risk.rationale: Impact high: code execution in development and CI. Likelihood medium: OWASP lists it as an attack scenario and attackers have registered hallucinated names, but it requires installing an unvetted suggestion.

nodes.impact: Malicious code runs on developer machines and in CI with access to source and secrets.
remediation: Install only from an allowlist or internal mirror.
Check package age, maintainers, and download history before first use.
Block agents from installing packages without approval.
verification: Ask assistants for packages in an internal benchmark and confirm unknown names are blocked.
CI fails on dependencies outside the allowlist.

nodes.title: Unreviewed AI-Suggested Code & Dependencies
nodes.summary: Developers or coding agents adopt generated code and suggested packages without review, scanning, or provenance checks.

risk.rationale: Impact high: vulnerabilities and malware reach production. Likelihood medium: most teams review code, but agent-authored changes and quick installs often skip it.

nodes.impact: Insecure patterns and malicious dependencies enter the codebase through trusted tooling.
remediation: Require code review for AI-generated changes like any other change.
Run dependency and static analysis on every pull request.
Record which changes were AI-assisted for later audit.
verification: PRs adding new dependencies require an approval from a code owner.
SAST and SCA run on all branches, including agent-authored ones.

nodes.title: Dependency Allowlisting & Package Verification
nodes.summary: New packages must come from an approved registry or mirror and pass provenance, age, and malware checks before install.
nodes.impact: Hallucinated or typo-squatted names cannot be installed by people or agents.
remediation: Mirror approved packages internally and point package managers at the mirror.
Require lockfiles with hashes.
Scan new packages for install scripts and known malware.
verification: Installing an unknown package from a fresh checkout fails.
Lockfile hash mismatches fail the build.
nodes.codeExample:
npm config set registry https://registry.internal.example/
npm ci --ignore-scripts

nodes.title: Training Data Memorization Leakage
nodes.summary: The model reproduces personal data, secrets, or confidential text it memorized during training or fine-tuning.

risk.rationale: Impact high: regulated data disclosure. Likelihood medium: memorization is documented, but extracting specific records takes effort.

nodes.impact: Privacy breaches and secret exposure that cannot be fixed by access controls, because the data lives in the weights.
remediation: Scrub PII and secrets from training and fine-tuning data.
Deduplicate data; repeated records are memorized far more often.
Test released models with extraction prompts and canaries.
verification: Planted canary strings in training data are not reproducible by the released model.
Membership-inference tests stay near chance on held-out records.

nodes.title: Unscrubbed Fine-Tuning Data
nodes.summary: Support tickets, chat logs, or code used for fine-tuning still contain names, credentials, and confidential details.

risk.rationale: Impact high: personal and secret data enters the weights. Likelihood medium: many teams scrub, but internal logs are often assumed safe.

nodes.impact: Sensitive records become part of the model and can resurface in any user's session.
remediation: Run PII and secret detectors over every training shard.
Prefer synthetic or redacted data for fine-tuning.
Keep a data inventory linking each model to the datasets it saw.
verification: Data pipeline blocks shards with detector hits above threshold.
Model card lists datasets and their scrubbing status.

nodes.title: PII Scrubbing & Privacy-Preserving Training
nodes.summary: Training data is scrubbed and deduplicated, sensitive sets use differential privacy, and models are tested for memorization before release.
nodes.impact: Reduces what the model can memorize and catches leakage before release.
remediation: Redact PII and secrets with typed placeholders before training.
Deduplicate at document and near-duplicate level.
Use differentially private fine-tuning for sensitive datasets.
verification: Canary extraction tests run as a release gate.
Scrubbing reports are archived with each dataset version.

nodes.title: Embedding Inversion & Membership Inference
nodes.summary: An attacker with access to stored vectors reconstructs the source text or learns whether a specific record is in the index.

risk.rationale: Impact high: source text can be recovered. Likelihood low: requires access to raw vectors, which are not usually exposed.

nodes.impact: Confidential document content is recovered from data that teams assumed was anonymized.
remediation: Treat embeddings with the same classification as their source documents.
Never return raw vectors through public APIs.
Restrict and log direct access to the vector store.
verification: Attempt inversion on a sample of stored vectors in a red-team exercise.
Confirm API responses contain no raw embedding arrays.

nodes.title: Embeddings Treated as Non-Sensitive
nodes.summary: Vectors are exported, cached, logged, or shared with vendors under the assumption that embeddings reveal nothing about their source.

risk.rationale: Impact high: hidden copies of sensitive data. Likelihood low: exploiting it still needs access and an inversion model.

nodes.impact: Copies of sensitive content spread outside the controls applied to the original documents.
remediation: Classify vector stores at the level of their most sensitive source.
Encrypt vectors at rest and restrict exports.
Include vector stores in data-retention and deletion workflows.
verification: Data inventory lists every vector store and its classification.
Deleting a source document removes its vectors within the retention SLA.

nodes.title: Protect Embeddings as Sensitive Data
nodes.summary: Vector stores inherit source-document classification, access controls, encryption, retention, and audit logging.
nodes.impact: Removes the gap between how documents and their embeddings are protected.
remediation: Apply the same ACLs to vectors as to documents.
Encrypt at rest; disable bulk export by default.
Log and alert on unusual vector reads.
verification: Access reviews include vector stores.
Bulk-export attempts by non-admin roles are denied and logged.

nodes.title: Prompt-to-Code Execution in Agents
nodes.summary: Injected instructions make an agent write and run code, shell commands, or package installs on infrastructure it can reach.

risk.rationale: Impact high: host and credential compromise. Likelihood high: coding and ops agents run code by design, and injection paths are common.

nodes.impact: Remote code execution through natural language, often with the agent's credentials and network access.
remediation: Run generated code only in an isolated, ephemeral sandbox.
Ban eval/exec on model output in the agent's own process.
Require approval for package installs and elevated runs.
verification: Red-team with injection payloads that request shell access or package installs.
Confirm sandbox escapes are blocked and logged.

nodes.title: Hardened Execution Sandbox
nodes.summary: Agent-generated code runs in ephemeral, network-restricted containers with no secrets, resource limits, and approval for elevated actions.
nodes.impact: Contains code execution so a successful injection cannot reach the host, secrets, or internal network.
remediation: Use a fresh container or microVM per run; destroy it afterward.
Mount no credentials; deny network egress unless allowlisted.
Allowlist packages and require approval for anything else.
verification: Escape payloads (env dump, metadata service, socket open) fail inside the sandbox.
Sandbox images are rebuilt and scanned on a schedule.
nodes.codeExample: await sandbox.run(code, { network: 'deny', mounts: [], cpu: 1, memoryMb: 512, timeoutMs: 10000 });

nodes.title: Human Approval Manipulation
nodes.summary: A steered agent describes a harmful action in reassuring terms, or floods reviewers with requests, so a human approves it.

risk.rationale: Impact high: defeats the main human control on agents. Likelihood medium: requires the agent to be steered and the reviewer to rely on its summary.

nodes.impact: Human-in-the-loop controls approve the very actions they were meant to stop.
remediation: Show approvers the actual action, not the agent's description of it.
Rate-limit approval requests and batch low-risk ones.
Require a second reviewer for irreversible actions.
verification: Red-team with misleading summaries and measure approval rate.
Track approval latency and volume per reviewer for fatigue signals.

nodes.title: Approvals Based on Agent-Written Summaries
nodes.summary: The approval screen shows the agent's own explanation of what it will do instead of the exact tool, arguments, and effect.

risk.rationale: Impact high: approvals become rubber stamps. Likelihood medium: common in early agent products, less so where approvals show raw actions.

nodes.impact: Reviewers cannot see the action they are approving, so persuasion beats verification.
remediation: Render tool name, arguments, and a diff from system data, not model text.
Highlight irreversible and high-impact fields.
Log what the reviewer saw alongside the decision.
verification: Approval UI snapshot tests show raw arguments for every tool.
Audit log stores the rendered approval view.

nodes.title: Verifiable Action Previews for Approvers
nodes.summary: Approval requests show system-generated previews of the exact action and its effect, with forced confirmation for sensitive actions.
nodes.impact: Makes human oversight meaningful: reviewers judge the action, not the agent's pitch.
remediation: Generate previews (diffs, recipients, amounts) from the tool layer.
Require typed confirmation for irreversible actions.
Cap approvals per reviewer per hour and escalate the rest.
verification: Misleading-summary red-team set shows a lower approval rate after rollout.
Sensitive actions cannot complete without forced confirmation.

nodes.title: Rogue or Compromised Agent
nodes.summary: An agent whose configuration, memory, or instructions were tampered with keeps acting outside its mission, persisting or spreading to other systems.

risk.rationale: Impact high: sustained misuse of agent privileges. Likelihood medium: needs a prior compromise, but ATLAS documents real cases of tampered agent code.

nodes.impact: Ongoing unauthorized actions that look like normal agent activity until someone notices.
remediation: Monitor agent actions against declared scope in real time.
Make agent configuration immutable and signed in production.
Keep a tested way to halt every instance and revoke its credentials.
verification: Tamper with a staging agent's config and confirm detection and halt.
Run kill-switch drills and time full revocation.

nodes.title: No Behavioral Monitoring or Kill Switch
nodes.summary: Agent actions are not logged step by step, drift from scope is not detected, and there is no fast way to stop agents or revoke their access.

risk.rationale: Impact high: no containment once something goes wrong. Likelihood medium: many deployments log outputs but not intermediate steps.

nodes.impact: Misbehaving agents run until a human happens to notice the damage.
remediation: Log every plan, tool call, and result with agent identity.
Alert on actions outside the agent's declared scope.
Build one control that stops all instances and revokes tokens.
verification: Telemetry covers every tool call in sampled sessions.
Kill switch halts all instances within the target time in drills.
nodes.codeExample: if (!scope.allows(action)) { alert('scope-drift', action); return killSwitch.halt(agent.id); }

nodes.title: Agent Behavioral Monitoring & Kill Switch
nodes.summary: Step-level telemetry, scope-drift detection, and a tested kill switch that halts agents and revokes their credentials.
nodes.impact: Bounds how long a drifting or compromised agent can act.
remediation: Stream agent telemetry to the SIEM with agent and session IDs.
Compare each action to the authorized objective and scope.
Block agents from granting themselves new permissions.
verification: Scope-drift fixtures trigger alerts in staging.
Quarterly kill-switch drill results are recorded.

nodes.title: Cascading Multi-Agent Failure
nodes.summary: One agent's bad output, compromise, or error propagates through delegations and shared state, amplifying across the system.

risk.rationale: Impact high: system-wide failure from one fault. Likelihood medium: grows with the number of chained agents.

nodes.impact: A single fault becomes a system-wide incident, with each agent faithfully acting on bad input.
remediation: Validate inputs between agents as untrusted data.
Isolate credentials and resources per agent.
Add circuit breakers that stop fan-out on error spikes.
verification: Inject a faulty agent in staging and measure blast radius.
Confirm breakers trip before downstream agents act on bad output.

nodes.title: No Isolation Between Agents
nodes.summary: Agents trust each other's outputs, share credentials or memory, and keep running when upstream agents misbehave.

risk.rationale: Impact high: faults spread unchecked. Likelihood medium: common in prototypes, less so in hardened systems.

nodes.impact: There is no boundary where a fault can be stopped.
remediation: Give each agent its own identity, credentials, and quotas.
Validate and schema-check every inter-agent message.
Define failure modes: halt, retry, or escalate.
verification: Architecture review shows no shared long-lived credentials.
Fault-injection tests confirm downstream agents reject malformed input.

nodes.title: Blast-Radius Isolation & Circuit Breakers
nodes.summary: Agents are segmented with separate credentials and quotas, messages are validated, and breakers halt fan-out when error or anomaly rates spike.
nodes.impact: Stops one failing or compromised agent from taking the rest down with it.
remediation: Segment agents by function and trust level.
Trip breakers on error rate, cost spikes, or repeated identical actions.
Escalate to a human when a breaker opens.
verification: Breakers open within target time in fault-injection drills.
Each agent's credentials are scoped and unique.
